title: Chapter 230: Surprise!
html:
“Was it this room?” The visitors entered Room 3, but it was empty.

“Are you sure you didn’t imagine it?” Supporting Guo Miao, Song An searched the room. There was nowhere for anyone to hide.

“I saw a face! He wore a doctor’s coat, and his face was stitched together. He appeared for an instant, then vanished back into the room.” Su Luoluo was certain. While everyone else had focused on Room 10, she had been watching the corridor behind them.

“Forget it. Stop searching,” Guo Miao said weakly, his legs still unsteady. “Let’s get out of here.”

“That’s impossible. I kept my eyes on Room 3, and the face never appeared again. He must still be in here.” Su Luoluo grabbed Xiao Du’s arm. “You were in the corridor too. Did you see anything?”

“Maybe. I’m not sure.” Xiao Du’s answer was maddeningly vague. They lingered for a while longer, then retraced their steps and prepared to leave.

They’re leaving already?Chen Ge emerged from the secret passage and followed the group. So be it. Their fans are waiting outside. I’ll let them keep some dignity.

He entered Room 10. When the hidden mission was triggered, they were inside this room.

Everything appeared normal apart from several footprints on the mattresses. While inspecting them, Chen Ge noticed a subtle change in the embedded face. He crouched, reached into its mouth, and pulled out a flyer.

Looks like they found this.

Chen Ge pocketed the flyer and entered the restroom opposite the electrotherapy room. He emerged carrying a female mannequin, dressed it in the Faceless Nurse’s uniform, and prepared one final surprise for the visitors.

As Chen Ge left Room 10, he heard movement in the third corridor. A glance revealed the person following him, but he gave no sign that he had noticed her. He rounded the corner, leaned against the wall, and waited. Several seconds later, soft, cautious footsteps approached.

The footsteps hugged the wall. In the dark corridor, danger could come from any direction, and only the solid wall offered her a sense of safety. The two drew closer with the corner blocking them from each other’s view. Afraid that Chen Ge might still be nearby, his pursuer did not round it at once. Instead, she adopted almost the same posture as he had—back against the cracked wall, legs tense, upper body inclined forward. Bending at the waist, she silently edged her face past the corner.

“Are you looking for me?”

Their eyes met, and Ye Xiaoxin’s breath stopped. Her heart hammered; blood rushed to her head, and her ears rang until she could hear nothing else.

Her temperature plunged, and she began to tremble. Chen Ge looked down at the short-haired woman, his stitched face twisting slightly. Without a word, he raised the hammer.

BANG!

The hammer struck the wall two meters above her head. Plaster shattered, showering her face with debris and proving that this was no dream. Ye Xiaoxin’s composure broke. Blood drained from her face as she spun and sprinted toward Room 3.

“Wait! Don’t run!” Chen Ge maintained a steady distance—neither catching her nor slowing down. His hammer scraped along the wall, and the sound chilled Ye Xiaoxin’s heart. She did not dare look back. A single thought filled her mind: Run!

She dashed into Room 3’s secret passageway, and Chen Ge followed closely behind her.

One fled; the other pursued.

They passed through the tunnel in the blink of an eye and exited at the director’s office.

The other visitors waited in the corridor, unaware of what had happened, though they could hear strange noises echoing through the surrounding sickrooms.

“Boss, I have a bad feeling. Something is coming.” Supporting Guo Miao, Song An repeatedly glanced over his shoulder.

“There are so many of us. Whatever comes, we have nothing to fear.” Guo Miao tried to bolster morale, but before he could finish, a disheveled woman burst from the director’s office. It was Ye Xiaoxin. The sight of the group stopped her short, and she screamed, “He’s coming for us! Run! Run for your lives!”

Her face was flushed from lack of oxygen. She looked nothing like the composed reviewer who had entered the Haunted House.

“He? Who is he?”

After delivering her warning, Ye Xiaoxin fled. One second later, brute force blasted the half-open door of the director’s office wide.

The door slammed into the wall and splintered. The first thing the visitors saw was a bloodstained hammer.

Chen Ge emerged from the director’s office in his bloodied coat. He had been pursuing Ye Xiaoxin but found Guo Miao’s group instead. Blocking their only exit, he turned toward them. “What a coincidence.”

His emotionless eyes sent chills down their spines. Before Chen Ge could move again, Su Luoluo and Xiao Du screamed and fled deeper into the Third Sick Hall.

“Hold your ground...” Guo Miao began, reaching out only to grasp empty air. Song An, who had been supporting him, had abandoned him and raced after Su Luoluo and Xiao Du. He was already several meters away.

“No matter the circumstances, abandoning your friend is wrong.” His decision made, Chen Ge ran past Guo Miao and pursued the fleeing three. The smell of blood swept by, and Guo Miao slowly slid down the wall. Watching Chen Ge recede, he drew a deep breath and began crawling toward the Haunted House’s entrance. “The truth cannot be buried. Someone has to escape this place alive...”

The fourth corridor ended in a dead end—and it was there that Chen Ge had placed the most traps. The visitors had been frightened before they properly explored the corridor, leaving many of its scare points untouched.

Chen Ge’s pursuit placed them under crushing pressure. By the time the three reached the dead end, they were near collapse.

“There’s no way out!” Xiao Du struck the wall veined with blood vessels, unable to put his terror into words.

“We’re trapped.” Song An’s face was equally filled with despair.

Of the three, Su Luoluo remained the calmest. “There must be a hidden passage. Remember? I saw a face inside Room 3, but when we searched, no one was there. I think there’s a secret entrance in that room.”

“Room 3?” They exchanged glances and decided to gamble. The three charged toward Chen Ge, then ducked into Room 3 just before reaching him.

“There really is a secret passage!” While pursuing Ye Xiaoxin, Chen Ge had forgotten to close the panel embedded in the wall, allowing the visitors to find the entrance at once.

“We’re saved!” Before they could be relieved, Chen Ge appeared at the door. “Hey!”

“Run!” Su Luoluo entered the tunnel first, with Xiao Du and Song An close behind. The dark passage admitted only one person at a time. When Su Luoluo saw the exit drawing near, her heart rose into her throat. Freedom was almost within reach.

She crawled faster. When she came within a meter of the exit, a bandaged face appeared at the other end of the tunnel.

The figure wore a bloodstained nurse’s uniform, and a woman’s giggle seemed to emanate from it. “What is that?”

Su Luoluo nearly cursed. She tried to stop, but her momentum carried her into the monster. Its lifelike head tumbled against her chest. The bandages loosened, revealing a strangely beautiful face. Then came the worst part: the impact fractured the nurse’s features, and the face shattered before Su Luoluo’s eyes.

“Ahhh!”

She tried to crawl backward while Xiao Du and Song An charged blindly forward. All three slammed together with a tremendous crash. Tangled in the cramped tunnel, they became hopelessly wedged in its center.

At the sight, Chen Ge chuckled and approached with his hammer. “Why are you doing this to yourselves?”
